reading.purpose: A ticket's description in the 1180px reading column.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Menus, popovers and toasts only (--shadow). Light mode: rgba(15,20,30,0.18). Never on modals: the bundled WebKitGTK 2.50 redraws a blurred shadow on every repaint under it.

shadows.name: working-glow
shadows.value: filter: drop-shadow(0 0 5px color-mix(in srgb, var(--g2) 45%, transparent))
shadows.purpose: Agent Working Rule only: rainbow text and icons (4px on the working dot). Never on any other element.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Behind a modal (--scrim); light mode rgba(30,30,36,0.32). The modal itself is a hairline panel with no shadow.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: All transitions (--ease). No spring, no bounce.

motion.name: t
motion.purpose: Things that appear, such as the selected card fading in (--t).

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons give a pixel when pressed.

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: Agent working dot; off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: glow-name
motion.purpose: Agent Working Rule: rainbow gradient flowing through working text; off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: glow-stroke
motion.value: 8s steps(96) infinite, color g1 > g2 > g3 > g4
motion.purpose: Agent Working Rule: icon stroke and working dot colour cycle; off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: think
motion.purpose: Agents panel thinking dots; off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: modal-in
motion.purpose: A dialog rises 4px and settles; the scrim fades in over the same 160ms.

mapLines.name: route

mapLines.name: link

mapLines.name: trunk

narrative.overview:
Slate night. The app is one cool monochrome field, slate fading to black, that a developer keeps open beside their editor all day. Nothing on it is decorative: white (ink, in light mode) is the only control colour of its default theme and the selection and focus colour of every theme, hue appears only when it means something, and the headline objects (release versions, ahead/behind counts) speak in a tall condensed display face. Everything else is quiet Inter and JetBrains Mono on hairline-ruled panels with 2 to 3px corners.

It replaces a look built from per-role hues (trunk orange, release violet, props cyan, selection blue), pills and glows. One piece of that look stays by owner decision: the flowing rainbow on anything an agent is working on, the one signal the owner loves and the one place the old hues and glow survive. The views, layout and behaviour of the app do not change; only this visual layer does.

The palette ships as one theme family, **Gitnetix Black & White** (`gitnetix-bw`) and **Gitnetix Black & White Light** (`gitnetix-bw-light`), in `src/lib/themes.ts`: every step is set exactly in the theme's `own` map. It is the default for new users (`DEFAULT_THEME`) and the pair "System" follows (`SYSTEM`). Gitnetix Dark and Gitnetix Light keep their own palettes in `app.css`, and the 34 third-party themes keep theirs through `tokens()`; all of them take this system's shapes, type, hairlines, map structure and neutral roles. The colour tokens below are the Black & White pair.

The approved reference is `.impeccable/mocks/slate-direction.html` (branch map and branch workspace at 1920x1080, each with the agents panel docked right, dark and light). Inside this world the branch map reads as a line diagram: one hairline trunk carries the shipped releases as stations, branches hang off it as small boxes (a header and one info row), ahead/behind rides on the incoming line as a small chip, and their commits float free beneath them.
keyCharacteristics: Cool slate-to-black ground, panels one step up, 1px hairlines.
Branch map as a station line: hairline trunk, ring stations, two-row boxes, ahead/behind chips on the lines, floating commits.
Pull requests read as the same line: ring stations by state in the list, and each pull request's checks, review and conversations as stations on its way to the base.
Tickets read like a page: one-line rows with a status ring, a 1180px reading column, and the ticket's way to a release as a station line in the margin.
Submodules read as a pin line: the pinned, checked-out and remote-tip commits as stops on one hairline, each action under the stop it moves the submodule to.
Dialogs read as a route sheet: the operation drawn as a route under the title, labelled rows in a 100px label column, the steps it runs as stops on a rail, buttons at natural width on the right.
White controls: solid white primary, 1px outline secondary; a dialog's last footer button fills red when it throws work away.
Hue only for diff add/delete, warnings and conflicts, plus the flowing rainbow on agent work.
Tall condensed numerals and versions; tracked small-caps labels.
Thin 1.25px icon strokes; hard, short motion.

rules.name: The Control Rule
rules.body: Ink (`--fg`) means "this is yours": selection, the active tab, segment and tag, check fills and focus, in every theme. `--accent` means "you can press this" and marks controls only: primary buttons, links and a few control states. In Black & White the accent is white (ink in light), so ink is the only control colour; Gitnetix Dark/Light and the third-party themes keep their own accent as their control colour. Never spend an accent on selection, focus, roles or status.

rules.name: The Meaning Rule
rules.body: Branch type, trunk, release, props and people carry no hue. Type reads as a text label (FEAT, FIX); trunk and release read by position and the display face. Names carry no hue either, like branch types and labels: an avatar without a picture is the same neutral disc for everyone. A hue on screen must answer "added, deleted, warning or conflict", or be the Agent Working rainbow.

rules.name: The Agent Working Rule
rules.body: Anything an agent is working on flows with the incumbent rainbow, and nothing else may. Text gets weight 600, a 90deg gradient of g1, g2, g3, g4, g1 at 300% size clipped to the text, flowing in 8s `steps(384)`, with no glow (the colour change is enough). Icons cycle their stroke through g1, g2, g3, g4 in 8s `steps(96)` with a `drop-shadow(0 0 5px)` of g2 at 45%; the working dot blinks and cycles the same way, with no glow. It appears on the top bar's Worktrees & agents icon, the project tab's dot while agents run, a branch box's "Claude working" info row, the selected card's Agent value, the focus head's agent pill, the agents panel's session dot and the current commit's station in the AI rebase dialog (an 11px disc cycling g1 to g4 in 8s `steps(96)`, no glow; Delete once the rebase stops). A waiting agent is Warn, never rainbow. Reduced motion stops all three animations and leaves the colours still.

rules.name: The Theme Rule
rules.body: Black & White is the default and what System follows; every other theme (Gitnetix Dark/Light in `app.css`, the 34 third-party themes through `tokens()` in `src/lib/themes.ts`) keeps its own ground, panel, text and accent, gets the derived steps (`--line2`, `--link`, `--ground`, `--route`, `--g1` to `--g4`) mixed from its colours unless it sets them, and takes the same shapes, type, hairlines and map structure. A third-party theme sets its raised, selected, hairline and status colours from its own palette in the palette's own roles (`own`); a colour under the floors (muted 4.5:1, faint 4:1, status and link text 4.5:1 on light panels and 4:1 on dark ones) only moves lighter or darker. Role hues are neutral in every theme: no component reads `--trunk-fg`, `--release-fg`, `--prop-fg` or `--mod-fg` for a role (`tokens()` still emits them for the marketing website, syntax highlighting and the agent-working rainbow read them).

rules.name: The One Loud Voice Rule
rules.body: Antonio is used only for screen and page titles, the welcome heading, the next release and headline numerals. Shipped versions read in Mono. Never Antonio for body, buttons, labels or branch names.

rules.name: The Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono is for what a machine hands back: paths, SHAs, refs, URLs and code, plus the Count role's tabular numbers and key caps. Plain words are never Mono: menu hints, captions and sentences are Inter, and a hint or sentence that holds a SHA or path wraps only that string in Mono (the menus' Copy SHA hint, the stale-remote box's submodule names).

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every map line is a hairline. The route from the trunk to the checked-out branch is 1.5px in the route colour (control white, ink in light mode); every other link is a 1px Link Dim curve; a falling-behind branch's link is dashed 3/4. No thick transit lines, no hue on the route, no pulse travelling along it, no glow. A one-line legend box floats at the canvas's bottom left (8px in, 16px up; 1px hairline-strong border, 3px corners, ground at 85%, padding 6px 12px, Inter 12px muted) with the route, other lines, falling behind and the line chip. Keys that don't fit wrap out of sight, never cut in half, and a "See all" link lists them in a 360px modal. It stops short of the selected branch's side column.

rules.name: The Station Action Rule
rules.body: On a station line each action sits under the stop it moves the subject to, and exactly one white primary goes on the stop that fixes the state; every other action there is a small outlined button.

rules.name: The Route Rule
rules.body: A dialog shows the operation before its form: the route of what moves where in its head, the steps it runs as stops, then labelled rows, and exactly one loud control, last in the footer.

dos: Do use ink for selection and focus in every theme, and `--accent` only for controls (white in Black & White).
Do show a disabled primary as the outline with a faint label.
Do show branch type, trunk and release by label, position and type, not hue.
Do keep colour for add, delete, warn and conflict only.
Do set screen and page titles, the next release and headline numbers in Antonio, everything else (shipped versions included) in Inter and JetBrains Mono.
Do keep every view, control and behaviour exactly where it is today.
Do draw the branch map in hairlines: 1.5px route, 1px other links, dashed 3/4 when falling behind, 1px faint trunk.
Do keep branch boxes to a header row and one info row, and let commits float beneath them with no container.
Do put ahead/behind on the incoming line as a chip, a rebase button when there is a behind count.
Do put shipped releases on the trunk as ring stations at an even 36px pitch, `main` as the large station where the route starts.
Do mark everything an agent is working on with the flowing rainbow (the Agent Working Rule), and stop it under reduced motion.
Do dock the agents panel right at 460px in both views.
Do put each action under the station it moves the subject to, with exactly one white primary on the station that fixes the state.
Do set menu hints, captions and sentences in Inter, and wrap only a SHA, path, ref or URL inside them in Mono.
Do draw a dialog's operation as a route under its title, its steps as stops, and its form as labelled rows with a 100px label column.
Do end a dialog footer with Back then one loud control at natural width: the white primary, or the filled red button when the dialog throws work away.
donts: Don't use gradient text, glows, coloured halos or drop-shadow filters, except the rainbow on agent work under the Agent Working Rule.
Don't use the working hues for anything but an agent working; a waiting agent is Warn.
Don't use pills (999px radius) or radii above 3px on rectangles.
Don't give branch types, roles or sections their own hue.
Don't use spring or bounce easing; motion is short ease-out, under 200ms.
Don't put a shadow on a resting surface.
Don't draw thick transit lines or a coloured route on the branch map; the red route of the trunk reference is not adopted.
Don't put commits inside a branch box or wrap them in a card on the map.
Don't put ahead/behind inside the box, or a separate rebase button under the commits.
Don't put a coloured side bar on a box, note or callout; a note is a hairline row with a leading icon.
Don't stretch dialog footer buttons to equal widths or stack field labels above their controls in a dialog, except on phones.
Don't fill a red button anywhere but the last place in a dialog footer; elsewhere destructive stays the outline with red text.
Don't put a shadow on a modal; it is a hairline panel over the scrim.
